scope: Public-ready editorial intelligence inputs for the first Bay Area pilot districts. Not yet wired into page generation.

districts.heading: How to read Downtown Oakland
districts.headline: East Bay institutional business core with BART access, civic adjacency, and professional office depth.
districts.opening_statement: Downtown Oakland is the East Bay's formal business core: civic institutions, BART access, professional office buildings, and older downtown blocks clustered around Broadway and City Center.
paragraphs: It fits organizations that want regional transit access, public-sector or nonprofit adjacency, and a more practical East Bay alternative to San Francisco's Financial District.
Compared with Uptown, Downtown Oakland reads more institutional and office-oriented. Compared with Jack London Square, it is less waterfront and more civic and transit focused.
best_fit: Teams comparing Oakland with San Francisco CBD options
districts.access_pattern: BART-first downtown access with strong East Bay and San Francisco comparison value.
editorial_guardrails: Do not present raw counts publicly.
Do not use current availability language from historical listing rows.
Do not include source or confidence language.

districts.commercial_identity: Mixed-use Oakland office and arts-adjacent district
districts.heading: How to read Uptown Oakland
districts.headline: Mixed-use Oakland office district for smaller-company, arts-adjacent, and transit-oriented teams.
districts.opening_statement: Uptown Oakland is the more mixed-use counterpart to Downtown Oakland, with office buildings, arts venues, food, apartments, BART access, and Lake Merritt-adjacent commercial blocks sharing a tighter urban setting.
paragraphs: It works for teams that want East Bay access and professional office options without the formality of the civic downtown core.

Compared with Downtown Oakland, Uptown feels less institutional and more mixed-use. Compared with Jack London Square, it is less waterfront and more Broadway, Franklin, Webster, and Lake Merritt oriented.
best_fit: Teams seeking East Bay access with street-level context
Companies comparing formal downtown with mixed-use office settings
districts.access_pattern: BART-oriented East Bay access with a more mixed-use commercial feel than Downtown Oakland.
editorial_guardrails: Do not make Uptown read like a second Downtown Oakland page.
Do not overstate adaptive reuse unless representative examples are added.
Keep source-concentration and boundary caveats internal.

districts.commercial_identity: Premium walkable Peninsula startup and professional downtown
districts.heading: How to read Downtown Palo Alto
districts.headline: Walkable Peninsula downtown for startup, professional service, and client-facing office users.
districts.opening_statement: Downtown Palo Alto is a compact Peninsula business district where low-rise office buildings, restaurants, retail, Caltrain access, and startup/professional-service demand sit close together.
paragraphs: It fits teams that want a walkable client-facing address rather than a campus or highway-corridor office setting.

Compared with Mountain View, Downtown Palo Alto is more downtown-oriented and client-facing. Compared with Redwood City, it is smaller and more tightly tied to startup, venture, and professional-service routines.
best_fit: Small and mid-sized downtown office users
Teams prioritizing walkability and Caltrain access
districts.access_pattern: Walkable downtown and Caltrain access, with stronger client-facing context than nearby R&D corridors.
editorial_guardrails: Do not blur the district with Stanford Research Park or California Avenue.
Do not use unsupported pricing or current availability claims.
